utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, you are to continue with the examination-in-chief. You have used 45 minutes. You have another hour and 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Thank you. I hope to be able to conclude in the time allocated to me. Before I continue, I just wanted to tell you that on Saturday I responded to Mr. Docherty's request, I responded by way of letter to the Prosecutor, in which I stated what it is they should show, meaning the photographs and documents we specified on our list.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Milosavljevic. You know where we left off last time. I tendered your report in which you stated clearly what sort of proof is needed to establish the presence of a victim at a crime scene; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: During your testimony you said that an external examination, be it on the spot or at the morgue or in some other place, is the minimum of things that need to be done in order for one to be able to provide an opinion as to the time and cause of death, as well as the mechanism of causing injury, especially in extraordinary circumstances such as in times of war. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You've also explained what it was that the police was supposed to do in order to secure the most important facts and items.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you specify what those most important things are that have to be carried out concerning external examination.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards external examination, first and foremost, one needs to look for and know how to recognise indicia of the time of death. After that one needs to describe the details found and photographs need to be taken, first and foremost, of the face, which has to be photographed from three different angles, as well as all other characteristics that may be of assistance when trying to establish the victim's identity. Then one also needs to examine all of the clothes and footwear, trying to find any defects, any damage, to the items. After clothes and footwear are removed, the body needs to be examined in order to see whether there are any traces of injuries and other marks that can be visible on the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Only after that can one go on about doing all of the other things concerning cause of death and other things that need to be done?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the bare minimum that is needed for us in order to be able to conduct any further analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All this that you've shared with us and all of the things you mentioned in your report concerning external examination which makes it possible for you to continue your work, in all of the cases you worked on from 1993 onwards, and we are talking about thousand of such external examinations, did you always do the very same thing as you described?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such external examinations were the minimum of all the things we needed to do. If possible we always tried to do more than that, including full autopsies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Are these the principles recognised by the discipline of forensic pathology all over the world in similar circumstances?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the scientific principles of conducting forensic analysis that all forensic pathologists are duty-bound to adhere to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us this, please: Is there such a thing as a code on the part of the International Red Cross when trying to prescribe the principles used in such circumstances, extraordinary circumstances, not only the war but floods and natural disasters, including crime scenes? Is there a code, not in the sense of regulation but a code of principles at the highest international level describing the procedure?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The International Red Cross is the very organisation which assembled all governmental and non-governmental experts when trying to establish certain recommendations, first and foremost, as part of which we also have the recommendations pertaining to carry out forensic examinations in circumstances such as these in which only external examinations are possible so as to collect the minimum of information which can be viewed as valid forensic proof.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: There is a document in existence - it is DD00-4626 - which is a document from an international gathering of experts that was organised by the ICRC. It contains 150 pages. It is an open-source document from the internet. I wanted to present it here so that you could tell us a few things concerning that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll repeat number. That is DD00-4626. Page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, on Friday the Chamber made a ruling as to those documents on the Defence list which counsel would be able to use in his direct examination of the witness. The document being referred to now, DD00-4626, 65 ter number 392D, is one of the ones that the Chamber excluded. There were some photographs and police reports that were permitted, as well as Dr. Milosavljevic's own report, but this particular document was excluded by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We didn't allow this document so that's excluded. Move on, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milosavljevic, all of the things you've said so far, absolutely all of it, is it in full accordance to the recommendations of the ICRC that were put in place in February 2002? And have you always followed those guidelines before and after that date?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of the things I said concerning external examinations, all of the facts that need to be established during such an examination can be also found in the recommendations made by a body comprising numerous international governmental and non-governmental experts. Some of my colleagues from my country participated in the work of that conference. All of the things I said about external examinations are to be found in that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Milosavljevic, you were able to see a large number of photographs from which I told you stem from another case that has to do with the indictment against Dragomir Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Based on those photographs alone, I asked you to give us your opinion as to whether you would be able to see -- to determine the place at which that person was killed or to establish the manner and cause of death. And based on those photographs alone, what was your answer? Did you find it possible to do that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I wanted to say that I saw 35 --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just a second. I was asking you in principle, based on those photographs that you saw and those photographs alone, were you able to determine anything that can tell us about the place where those people were killed?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And as you started answering, you said you saw 34 photographs on which there are victims alleged to have been killed by a 120-millimetre shell on the 28th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was able to see those photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the things you've described, based only on those photographs -- well, let me ask you this first: Were you able to reach any conclusions as to where those photographs were taken?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can presume that they were made at the morgue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on the morgue photographs and on the photographs showing blood traces from the scene, can you say for certain that the victims were at the spot which is alleged that they lost their lives at?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: On those photographs are there any victims for whom one can say for certain that they were not killed by shell shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How many victims in total would that be?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least in two cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: After I've shown you these photographs you will be able to confirm that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would please like the witness to be shown document DD00-4989. It's an integral part of 65 ter document 2595. These are the photographs of victims 46, 54, and 76, showing three victims from the list of victims from the Prosecution document P266, page 2, admitted into evidence through Witness W-14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Who was W-14? Would you remind us, if you can, in a public session. If not, we'll go into private.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to give you the full name, we need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown from this document, extracted from the 65 ter document, photograph number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milosavljevic, what can you assert in relation to this photograph and the person depicted in it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look carefully at this photograph, primarily the right-hand side, the top right-hand side of the photograph, that is, to the right of the head of the body of the deceased person, one can clearly see two next to each other and then two close together, and below the shoulder, if we zoom in, you can see another three pellets, the so-called shotgun pellets, which is the charge of bullets used with shotguns. So if we look carefully at the face, the left eyebrow closer to the nose, one can see a lump under the skin and the same lump can be seen on the tip of the nose. The similar lump can also be seen below the lower lip, the left-hand side of the lower lip. These lumps were caused by under-skin infiltration of shotgun pellets that you can see on the right-hand side of the photo. On the right-hand side of the lateral side of the neck one can see a wide circular wound. And bearing in mind all these features and characteristics and these shotgun pellets, one can say that this man --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Judge Harhoff has a query.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Doctor, I have a difficulty in actually seeing the things you say you see on this picture. Is it possible for you to indicate with an arrow or a circle on the photo just where these lumps are and the wound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the pellets that I mentioned at the beginning and these are the lumps and this is the wound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please, have you been able to examine this yourself on site or are you basing yourself only on this photograph to determine all this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't have an opportunity to visit the scene. I only had an opportunity to look at the photographs contained in the case file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So, Witness, you say what you see is evidence of shotgun pellets, not shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is it that you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we see shotgun pellets. Shrapnel looks completely different. These are regular round smooth pellets. Shrapnel is of a regular form, different sizes and shapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That was my question, what is the difference between shrapnel and pellets. Now, you have told us shrapnel is of a regular form, different size and shape. Would you be more specific? Perhaps could you indicate by drawing what it is that you would expect to see --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The witness said irregular form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Irregular, irregular form, I see. Could you indicate what it is that you would expect to see were it a shrapnel wound? Is that the drawing to the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is shrapnel up there and below that are the shapes of wounds caused by shrapnel. There is a photograph which clearly shows what I've just demonstrated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. So that's shrapnel and the wound caused from shrapnel. Would you just indicate by a drawing as well a pellet and the wound caused by a pellet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a pellet and the cartridge, of the bullet contains thousands of these pellets. So once it's fired from a relatively close range, a cluster of pellets can cause a rather large wound, round wound. Pieces of individual pellets which are not within this cluster and if the distance from the body is bigger, 40, 50 centimetres, individual pellets leave this cluster and can be found around the wound. They go under the skin and then they can be found as these lumps surrounding the wound. Based on the pellets and the look of the wound, together with the ballistics, we can establish a relative range of fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And you say that the wounds that you saw on this photograph were similar to those -- similar in shape to those that you have depicted at the bottom of this screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In my career I had an opportunity to see several hundreds of wounds caused by shotguns -- shotgun fire from various ranges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And what range would you say was applicable in the case of these wounds?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only give a rough estimate because it takes a ballistic and forensic expertise to establish the exact distance. But based on the position of the wound and the position of the pellets under the skin, the range shouldn't have exceeded 50 centimetres, or let's say circa 50 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In other words, a very close range.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In forensic terms it's a relative range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Doctor, let me just be clear that I understand you perfectly well. In your view, this witness which is shown on the picture was killed not by a mortar but by a shotgun at a distance of less than 1 metre. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: A shotgun would be lethal by bullets, I understand, and the bullet would have an entry wound and an exit wound as opposed to what we see here is the entry wound. The only thing that I would identify from this picture - I must say that the dissolution of the picture is poor - but there is this black spot on his left eyebrow which to me could be an entry wound of a bullet, but I'm not -- I can't -- I'm not sure what you're saying in respect of the lump on the nose and the lump under the left part of his lower lip, nor can I make out what the wound is on his neck. Can you please help me understand and to read this picture.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I have to say that this was a digital photograph with a lot of pixels in it, and you're quite right, it's not very clear. I had an opportunity to see the actual photo which shows more clearly that this is on the right-hand side of the neck and that this is possibly an entry wound. If you look on this pellet below the lower lip, above it there is a trace on the skin which resembles a lesion, a furrow lesion made by the pellet where it first goes on the surface of the skin and then entered the skin and remained under the lower lip. The one on the tip of the nose primarily by -- judging by its size, resembles the infiltrated pellet. And it's too small to be indicative of an entry wound caused by small arms, and such a wound has other characteristics that clearly distinguishes it from the pellet that has ended up under the skin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe it can better be seen if we put it on the ELMO, and we have one now on the ELMO. So if the doctor could kindly look at the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry. Let us hear Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand, of course, that the Chamber ruled on Friday that these photographs could be used, but I do want to point out for the record and also to object that we are hearing for the first time that it is this witness' opinion that victims at Markale died from being shot by shotguns and not by some other effect. It was not in the doctor's report, it was not in the supplemental letter that Mr. Tapuskovic sent to me on Saturday, and this is not -- this is simply not the way that things ought to be done. We should not be learning this expert's opinion for the first time during his direct examination and I object on that ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I won't exclude it. If you're embarrassed by hearing it for the first time, there are ways of dealing with it. There are ways of dealing with that. I'm interested in seeing that the truth be found and I will ensure that there is fairness in respect of both parties. Now, I wanted to ask the doctor whether from the photographs that he examined he saw victims who died from shrapnel wounds.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And would that be the case in respect of the victims represented by all the other photographs that you saw, apart from these three?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The victims shown on some of the photographs lack the external indications of injuries. On the photographs I was able to see, one cannot see those. They were photographed in their clothes. The pictures are of poor quality, such as this one. Therefore, on the clothes and parts of body that can be seen, one cannot see clear signs of injury. Also, on some of the victims, one is able to see shrapnel impact and other characteristics of an explosion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you have any of those photographs available?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Judge Robinson, the third photograph shows the very characteristics. This is what I wanted to show this expert in the end, since we have to analyse that as well. The third photograph shows that very thing. We have prepared that photograph. And as for Mr. Docherty, we told him two days ago that some victims seemed not to have been killed at Markale but elsewhere. They were simply not killed at Markale. We have notified my learned friend as to the nature of such injuries and it was clearly stated in our communication. In the two days that have lapsed they may have consulted a physician; they may have asked someone for some assistance. We told them clearly that at least in two cases, we have this physician's opinion that they were not killed at Markale but elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So you will be coming to evidence from photographs of victims killed by shrapnel. Well, I will leave you to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we have one such photograph that we wanted to present, and one can clearly see what a shrapnel wound looks like. For without that, the things referred to by the expert so far would not be sufficiently clear. There would be no way to compare that. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milosavljevic, on the left-hand side there is also a light spot on the photograph, to the left of the head.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you anything concerning that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If you believe that this photograph was taken at the morgue, what do you think where these pellets came from? How did they arrive in the morgue? It seems that they were on the ground under the body or next to it.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the position of the pellets we can only assume that they fell out of the exit wound. However, that part of the body was not photographed and is not in accordance with the forensic principles. The body was not disrobed either, and had that been done I would have been able to tell you much more clearly about the direction of fire and other issues that we are supposed to examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What are you trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These pellets may have fallen out of the exit canal of the wound during transport and the putting of the body on the autopsy table when the photographs were taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As for the marks on the face, they are caused by what?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The three lumps I mentioned are pieces of shrapnel which have penetrated subcutaneously to that part of the body. I said that in addition to the lesion below the left lip, one can see the trace left by the movement of shrapnel across that part of the face.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd like to tender this photograph with the markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D370, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty, the Chamber has been considering your position and in particular the Chamber has been considering the lateness of the notice given to you in respect of the evidence that we are now hearing and which is important at any rate in relation to these three victims. Are you in a position to say now whether you would be able to deal with that in your cross-examination or whether you would need more time to carry out consultations?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What I've heard so far, I think I could deal with in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show photograph number 4 to the witness from the set of photographs, DD00-4988.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milosavljevic, based on your experience in investigating crimes, this wound seen on this victim's body, would it be indicative to you of a wound of a different type if one were to seek any explanation on your part as to the cause of that wound?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at the wound carefully on the right side of the chest, the characteristics are as follows: There is a regular circular defect in the middle of the wound and there is an outer ring, the width of perhaps 2 to 3 millimetres. It is an abrasion. And in this specific case this could be the entry defect and the ring of the wound caused by a projectile fired from a small arm. Judging by the shape of the ring, the projectile probably came from the right-hand side and from above as to the position of the victim's body at the moment of injury.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Counsel, where was this photo taken? Is this from the morgue or is it on the spot?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Harhoff, not a single photograph that has to do with the Markale incident was taken at the scene. Not one. That is why this witness had more difficulty in assessing those photographs. This picture was taken at the morgue, as did the other photographs of other victims allegedly killed at Markale.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Before I move on to the third photograph I wanted to ask you this: You categorically stated based on your experience, having in mind the ring around the wound, that this is clear proof that this was actually a firearm bullet.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could only have been caused by a firearm. Shrapnel wounds are irregular in shape. They do not exhibit the bruise ring.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have something for the transcript. While we were discussing the previous victim, what was entered in the transcript was shrapnel and the witness kept saying or referring to shotgun pellets. And in one place what appeared was shrapnel, which he did not mention, not once. A piece of shrapnel is different from a shotgun pellet. And in the transcript we have "shrapnel."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness clearly stated, said "shrapnel" on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, if you are saying that there is an error in the translation and in relation to this issue which is of relative importance, you would have to point us to the precise line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 5, page 15, and line 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I do recall indeed that when the witness gave his reply, the interpretation we received appeared to say that there were traces of shrapnel found on the body of the first photograph victim and that confused me and I'm sure it was mentioned three or four times, the word "shrapnel," because if I understood the witness correctly, he was asserting that the witness on the first photo was killed not by shrapnel but by bullets, yet the interpretation kept on talking about shrapnel, which was confusing. But now that we are talking about the first photo, it confused me also that you said that these -- all three photos are taken from the morgue. The first photo showed bullet pellets on the wall, on the floor, on the ground next to the victim. Surely there wouldn't be traces of bullets in the morgue, would there?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Harhoff, I think it was mentioned that the expert thought that those pellets fell out of the wound once the body had been placed on the table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The question is for the witness to answer, not for you to give an explanation, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He's already told us about that, Your Honour. It didn't come from me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Then let him repeat it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that one of the possible explanations as to the presence of the pellets on the floor or on the table where the photographs were taken was that when the body was being transported and placed on the table, those pellets may have fallen out of the exit canal of the wound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm sure we'll see the picture again and I'll have a chance to have a second look. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning this photograph, can you tell me this: Had you had a photograph which had to have been taken during an external examination, it would have been of great assistance in making your conclusions.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that case we would have been able to see whether there is an entry/exit wound in this case or whether the projectile itself still remains buried in the body. If there is an exit wound, then we can be 100 per cent sure that it was actually a projectile that was fired, and in that case we would know what the direction of the wound canal is. Coupled with the characteristics visible at the place of entry, all this would be of much assistance to a ballistics expert when determining direction of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the traces that we can see here, you say definitely that this person was killed from a firearm.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to all the characteristics, this victim was killed by a fire -- a bullet fired from a small arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this photograph also be admitted into evidence. The next photograph is on page 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D371, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, if I understand you correctly, each time that a human body is touched or wounded by shrapnel, these do not come out; they stay buried within the body. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In principle shrapnel have smaller kinetic energy than the projectiles fired from small arms and they seldom exit the body. However, if the person was at a close range of the explosion and the travelling of shrapnel through the body is such that it hits bone structures that can absorb even the bullets fired from small arms, then exceptionally it may happen for shrapnel to penetrate and go through the body. But in the cases that I mentioned normally the travelling path through the body is very short. This usually happens with stomach cavity, thigh muscles, arm muscles, and things like that. Most often muscle structures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So in the case of a shot fired, for instance, at close range, there is an entry point and an exit point which may provide useful information to the ballistics expert regarding where the firing came from. Now, regarding shrapnel which exceptionally come out of the body, could the expert reach sufficiently clear conclusions as to the entry point and the exit point regarding shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. In case of shrapnel both the entry and exit wounds are similar by the way they look like - they are of irregular shape, of sharp edges - because shrapnel tears the tissue that it passes through because of its sharp edges, unlike a bullet which, due to its high kinetic energy and regular [Realtime transcript read in error "irregular"] shape, creates a regular mechanical penetration through the tissue that it passes through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 12, it should say that the bullet creates a regular shape, whereas in the transcript it says irregular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. That would seem to be correct. Thank you. Move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since this photograph has been admitted into evidence, I would now like now the Chamber to look at the wounds caused by shrapnel, and that's photograph number 2 in the document that we assigned the number DD00-4988.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milosavljevic, can you please explain to the Judges what you mentioned earlier about the wounds. What is the difference between the wound made by shrapnel? Does this photograph illustrate this enough for the Judges to understand it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph, in the right-hand half of the front stomach is one wound, and there's another wound, too, which clearly show that they are irregularly shaped with sharp edges and different sizes. One has a teardrop shape; the other one has a groove shape. It depends always on the shape of the shrapnel that was made as a result of detonation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions about this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless the Chamber has any further questions, I would like this photograph to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D372, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milosavljevic, for the previous two photographs we can say for sure that the wounds were not caused by shrapnel originating from a 120-millimetre shell.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first two photographs there is absolutely not a single indication in the wounds that could cast a shadow of a doubt that this was caused by shrapnel. Both victims' wounds show that they were caused from completely different weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me, in forensic terms, can -- a video footage can be used in the course of investigation as evidence?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said before that photographs and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, I don't understand the question. Can a video footage be used in the course of an investigation as evidence? How is he in a position to say what is or is not evidence? I don't find that helpful at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps my question was not precise enough. But, Your Honours, the witness has seen three videos and one of these videos is already admitted into evidence, and he can demonstrate here to you several things in this video, the most important one being how the scene -- crime was tampered with, how bodies were added to the crime scene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In forensic terms, can a video footage be significant in arriving at a conclusion about what actually happened in terms of establishing how the wounds were caused or the place where somebody got killed? So can a video footage be used in forensics for anyone who is authorised - and in this case, this is the Chamber - to draw conclusions?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both photographs and video footage are used as ancillary tools in forensics in order to provide better quality evidence of forensic procedure carried out by investigators and forensic examiners, both in situ and in the morgue. Both video footage and photographs are used as auxiliary tools to provide both better and documented evidence of what was done during the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not helped by that kind of evidence. It's not for him to say what I can use. He can say what are the advantages or disadvantages of a particular method of investigation, but it is not for him to say what the Chamber can rely on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Robinson, whatever I'm doing is kind of my modest assistance to you as a Defence lawyer. That is my sole purpose. And for that reason I asked the question -- I asked the witness this question. As an expert, after having seen this video, he can demonstrate to you the maximum number of casualties in this footage, but he can also show you which bodies were not there when an event took place or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show the witness this video so that you can see how the bodies were planted at the crime scene?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. This video is on the spreadsheet of documents that counsel wanted to use with this witness and in Friday's discussion it, too, was excluded from consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I did say, however, that the Chamber would review this matter when it came up. I don't see the -- any need for this, Mr. Tapuskovic. The Chamber will -- the Chamber will abide by the decision that it made. We'll not have the video shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I respect your decision, but the witness has claimed about two victims that they were not at the crime scene at all because they were not killed by shrapnel. And the video shows how the victims that had not been killed at that location were brought to this location. I'm definitely going to use this video in my closing argument and this witness can be of help in demonstrating positively to you how certain bodies were planted in the meantime. So this is related directly with the photographs that we were looking at before and that's the footage number 8623.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's not clear to me how you can use it in your closing argument if the Chamber has disallowed it, but I'm going to consider the matter with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Well, having consulted my colleagues, the Chamber will allow the video to be shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm going to use this in my closing argument because this is already a Prosecution exhibit, P623. There are another two videos that this expert has seen, but today I have decided to use this footage which already is admitted into evidence, P623. I would like you to look at it and pay particular attention to the first 1 minute and 30 or 40 seconds. While the video is being played, because there is no commentary in the video itself, the witness can describe what he's seeing, and after that we can address some other issues. If the witness is going to be allowed to comment on the video while it is being played --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, you must allow the witness to give the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please stop, please stop the film. [Interpretation] Can you please rewind to the beginning. [In English] Stop there. Okay. [Interpretation] If you look carefully on the surface, in the right-hand angle, there is something resembling a cardboard box. Close to it there are no victims. More further on we can see a car and on the left-hand side another car. So on this entire surface there were no casualties, there were no dead people lying on the ground in the vicinity of this object that resembles a cardboard box. Can we please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now you can see it even more clearly. The camera is coming closer to the scene. You can see a wounded person here. Then you can see a dead body here. You see a group of people both dead and wounded, a large number of them. Another wounded person is being carried away. We see a motorcycle rider on the left-hand side with a serious injury to the head. You can see a large number of casualties on the right-hand side of the screen. Now, the camera goes back that we saw earlier where there were no victims. There is the cardboard box and now you see a dead body that wasn't there a minute ago while the camera was shooting this particular area. So maybe we can rewind again to this particular segment of the footage. Some 15 seconds of the footage back. A little more, please. So you can see this cardboard box that we saw earlier and we saw that there were no casualties, but now we can see a dead body lying there. Now, if we go on, this footage shows a large number of casualties, both dead and wounded. Now you can see a convoy of cars in the background and beyond that spot there are no other casualties. So the casualties are slowly being evacuated. The normal procedure in forensics is not to allow any tampering with the scene in order to offer assistance to the casualties, but it is not customary to remove the bodies of the casualties from the scene before the arrival of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there is a mistake in the transcript. However, can we go back to the spot where the body of that woman is close to the cardboard box, and the witness can explain how is it possible that there is no blood around and under the body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let us do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one thing, please, for the transcript. On page 26, line 2, it says "to allow," to allow intervention on the crime site to help the victims, and in English it says it's "not to allow." So normally it would be "to allow" and the interpretation was "not to allow." The witness said that normally you can allow to help the victims, but what is not allowed, however, is to remove the deceased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see, yes. So it should be: "The normal procedure is to allow --" well, perhaps, tampering is not the right word, "to allow some intervention in the scene in order to offer assistance to the casualties, but it is not customary to remove the bodies from the scene before the arrival of the police." Yes, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If we could see this woman from up close.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can get a bit closer. A bit further more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What happened to this person?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see some blood on the lower part of the face and in the area of the nose. We also see some blood on the chest, or rather, on the clothes. We cannot tell anything about the nature of injuries, but in the area immediately next to the head and around the body there are no traces of blood. This is what can clearly be seen on the photograph. We also saw that the body of this woman was not in this place at the beginning of the footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Forensically speaking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And what is the conclusion you say you draw from this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a forensic expert, my conclusion is that this victim was not killed at this place. At the beginning of the footage this body was not there. Had she been killed in situ she would have been there. As to how the body ended up there I cannot say and I cannot tell you where it originates from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I be shown on the footage the cardboard box to which reference was made? Can you show us that, Court Deputy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the left-hand side, in the pedestrian area. This is it. It resembles a cardboard box.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, can I use the IT lingo and ask you to zoom in on that so I can see -- can it be shown more clearly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand that it can't be done. I would have to request one of the parties to produce a still. But I will be interested in seeing the cardboard box more clearly, the size and its other features.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: My colleague would like to see the video in its entirety again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Stop now. It's not clear to me. Are we to have seen in that video somebody carrying a box? No?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are past the time for the break so we'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have about 20 minutes left, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When reviewing the footage you gave some explanations and presented them to the Bench. When it comes to the woman lying next to the cardboard box, even if we put aside everything you've explained so far, of what importance is it that underneath the body and around it there is no blood whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually when there is a victim in situ, there are numerous traces, first of all, blood flowing out of the wounds sustained by the victim, and usually in a case like this when an explosion is concerned such blood loss is significant. Blood can be found on the surface, around the body, and underneath it; therefore, always there are blood traces indisputably telling us that that victim had actually been killed at the spot where found.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You explained what can be seen as the camera comes in closer and then you told us what you can see -- what the camera is showing us a minute later. You also mentioned additional two wounded people or killed. Was there any blood around them?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When talking about the two injured persons, the camera pans across too quickly and one cannot say whether there are or aren't any blood traces at the spot where the two injured persons are sitting on the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me this, please: Forensically speaking, everything that can be seen on the footage, what does it show as clear?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What one can clearly state when reviewing the footage is that there is a number of people who were killed or injured due to an explosion. There are injured people; there are killed people. By counting carefully we cannot determine an exact number, but one can estimate that the figure moves in the area of 25 to 30 people who were injured or killed. We can also try and guess at an area affected by the explosion at which people were killed or injured, since they were there at the time of explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions on that topic; therefore, I will move on and conclude with another topic. It has to do with document D19, and I was granted leave by the Chamber to use it. It has to do with the injuring of Dzenana Sokolovic and his child. Could we please see D19?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you like to have this video admitted? Oh, it's already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is P623.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's the Prosecution exhibit, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 623. But now let us look at D19, please, page 14, where the injuries on the child are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Before that, Witness, could you explain to the Judges this: You've told us a lot of things so far and you mentioned the minimum standard needed to make certain conclusions. Which medical document, during the course of any investigation that has to do with a murder, is of the greatest help in coming as close as possible to the truth?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most important forensic medical document is the autopsy finding. It should contain all relevant and necessary elements and facts with the weight of proof based on which one can carry out a valid forensic analysis and to respond to all possible questions concerning a specific incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As regards the 28th of August, at your disposal you did not have an autopsy finding for any of the victims.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the document before you. What can you tell us based on the things contained therein, what can you tell us about any aspects of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before me I have an excerpt from the autopsy file of Nermin Divovic. It was signed by assistant Dr. Ilijas Dobrac, who is specialised in forensic pathology, therefore he's a specialist. Contained therein is the case history in terms of the cause of death. We have transclopetarium capitis which means a gun-shot injury to the head. It says in the brackets that entry point was on the right cheek, exit point on the left side at the back of the head, which means that the direction of the canal of the wound moves from the left to the right and above to -- interpreter's correction: from below upwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go to page 11. Page 11. Please pay attention to the things that you deem important and that have to do with the issue discussed when talking about the killed boy. The statement contained in the document, what does it tell you? It was drafted by the persons who carried out the autopsy.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see here the page pertaining to Dzenana Sokolovic, who was injured. It is in this line. It says paramedially to the left one can see an entry wound the size of .5 centimetres, with some blood loss. Paramedially to the right, we can see the exit wound, the size of 2.5 centimetres, with blood loss. Could we please have the page back.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot see that translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is difficult to read. This in any case would mean that there is an entry/exit wound in the abdominal area, with an exit part on the left-hand side and the exit part on the right-hand side. The entry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, there must be some confusion in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely. On page 32, instead of first "exit part" it should be "entry part." So what was said in B/C/S was that the entry part is on the left-hand side and the exit part is on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That would seem to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We have the conclusion. What is the canal's direction compared to the level of the ground?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since both wounds are paramedially located, one on the left-hand side and one on the right-hand side, it means that the projectile had come from the left, went through the abdominal wall and exited on the right side. Since there is no data on the distance between the entry and exit part from the heel of the victim, we can presume that the surgeon probably believed that they are positioned symetrically compared to the heel of the person. That would mean that the projectile had come from the left to the right, moving parallel to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This entry/exit wound had this direction and you explained the direction of the entry/exit wound through the head of the killed boy, from below upwards, as you said. It entered in the cheek and exited above the ear. Can a correlation be established between these two exit/entry wounds? I'm not going to suggest anything to you, but can they be correlated and therefore can one can say that they were caused by one and the same bullet?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to this style of examination. This -- the location of these wounds has been the subject of a lot of testimony in this trial. Dr. Beslic, the surgeon who actually operated on Dzenana Sokolovic, testified by videolink from Sarajevo and explained all of this, and to go back to this anamnesis that was prepared in the casualty department when Ms. Sokolovic was brought in and to not present the witness with the surgeon's findings, the surgeon's testimony, the surgeon's report, the surgeon's re-examination of Ms. Sokolovic is, I put it, a very, very misleading way to proceed and I object to it being done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty, the Chamber is of the view that the question is not inadmissible because the witness has not seen those other pieces of evidence to which you have referred. You may bring that to the witness' attention in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Speaking of this, please, can the scars of an entry and exit wound -- wounds as described by you 12 years later bear any influence on the assessment that was recorded back in 1994 or 1995.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If one has a valid medical document from the time when the injury was inflicted, scars can in no way be used as a valid proof in order to qualify a wound. They particularly cannot be used in order to establish accurately which of the two scars relates to an entry and which relates to an exit wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But can you tell us, these two paths - as you described them, one of them was horizontal - what do they indicate?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The medical records which I used to draw at my previous conclusions clearly indicate that these two persons were injured by two different projectiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And my last question: Provided that the bullet had come from the right-hand side and provided it passed as it did through the entire abdomen of a person, would that bullet be capable of causing an injury or death by passing through the skull of another person?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The projectile that passed through the entire abdomen, which is approximately 50 centimetres at least in length, due to hydrokinetic properties of a human body as well as the ballistic properties of the bullet and the ballistic characteristics of the wound and the mode of behaviour of a bullet while passing through a human body, in this particular instance it loses a significant part of its kinetic energy and it also rotates in the process. Due to that the exit wound was 3 times 2 centimetres because the bullet exited laterally, turning towards the back side, and when this kind of bullet exits, hasn't [Realtime transcript read in error "has it"] got enough kinetic energy for piercing even the skin on the human body, let alone any bones.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, another thing. At page 34, line 19, in English it says "has it got" instead of "has got." It's the opposite. In English we have the opposite of what was said in B/C/S at that line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So the word "it" between "has" and "got" should be deleted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Has it got enough kinetic energy for piercing."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll say it. The word "it" should be deleted. So it should be "has got."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, "has not got."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you saying it should be "has not got"?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: It says "has got" in the transcript and it should be "has not got" enough kinetic energy to trans -- to pierce the skin on the human body. [Interpretation] It has "has got" and it should be "hasn't got".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. That is probably just a slight misdescription. "It" then should be "n't" got, "hasn't got." Yes, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Good morning, Doctor. You and I have not met before today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you understand that you prepared a report in this case which was turned over around the middle of July; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you would agree with me, wouldn't you, that most of what you have testified to today and on Friday was not in that report; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of it is in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: There is no discussion of the specifics of the Markale marketplace incident of 28th of August in your report, is there?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my report I spoke about the scene of crime. Since in the entire set of documents there is not a single valid forensic or medical document or report on the external examination --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Excuse me, that is not the question I asked you. I asked you if there was a specific discussion of the Markale marketplace killings in your report. I understand that there are general principles. I understand that you have attempted to apply those general principles here today and on Friday. But it's not in your report, is it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And the killing of Nermin Divovic and the wounding of his mother, Dzenana Sokolovic, is also not discussed specifically in your report, is it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Why did you make the decision not to put those things in your report?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already said, the documents given to me for analysis, I didn't find any relating to the Markale incident. I didn't find a single medical record relating to the injury or any external examination or an autopsy report relating to the fatalities of that incident. Therefore, I didn't have valid forensic documents on the basis of which I would be able to state an opinion on these incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: But today and a little bit on Friday you have drawn opinions concerning these incidents. You have used videos and photographs and, in the last incident, medical documents to do so. So when were you provided with those documents?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These documents were provided to me in late June of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So you had the documents concerning young Mr. Divovic and his mother, Dzenana Sokolovic, in late June, but you did not include that in your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And yet you do give an opinion about those documents here today, just a few minutes ago, don't you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So what happened to these documents to make them valid for forensic opinion between late June and this morning? If you could draw a conclusion from them this morning, why couldn't you draw a conclusion and put it in your report?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The medical records relating to the injuries sustained by Dzenana Sokolovic and then extracts from the autopsy reports regarding the killing of her son are documents that are valid and properly signed by experts, but they are not sufficient for a full forensic analysis in the manner that forensic analysis should be done, and that is to say, to provide all the answers that it's supposed to provide. In the medical document relating to Dzenana Sokolovic's injury, there is only one sentence which describes the location of the entry wound and the exit wound. Apart from that, there is no precise data relating to the distances between these two wounds and from the centre line leading to the heel of the person, which are necessary for us to provide and sign a forensic report which would give a precise direction of the path of the wound through the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Doctor, it's becoming a very long answer. So your view was that the documents were not sufficient for you to draw a forensic conclusion. Is that an accurate or a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: But you did offer a conclusion about 15 minutes ago, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only made a supposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I see. Another word for "supposition" in English, Doctor, would be "guess," wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we have here is a professional supposition. I can say exactly that this is an entry/exit wound in the abdomen. I can find where the entry point and the exit point is and what the direction is. However, as for other more accurate details, I am not able to provide them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Well, let's talk about what data you had at your disposal in order to make your supposition. We've seen Defence Exhibit 19, which are some police reports and some medical documentation. I take it that you had those documents at your disposal when you wrote your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And obviously, since they were put up on the screen in front of you, you had those documents when you testified here today; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did you see the statement of the surgeon who operated on Dzenana Sokolovic? His last name is Beslic.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw medical documents signed by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: But you did not see the statement that he provided and that was introduced into evidence at this Tribunal, did you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did you read the transcript of the testimony he gave when he, just like you, testified before this Tribunal about this case?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you know that Dr. Beslic performed a physical examination of Ms. Sokolovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these are the things that it is up to you to decide. I intentionally did not show him witness statement. This is not something for an expert witness to decide and weigh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I can't understand the basis for the objection. He's simply asking him whether he read the transcript of the testimony. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Were you aware that Dr. Beslic, at the request of the prosecutors in this case, physically examined Dzenana Sokolovic a second time at the Kosevo state hospital in Sarajevo? Were you aware of that until I asked you this question just now?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did you make any attempt to talk to the doctor who signed this short autopsy report concerning Nermin Divovic?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, although I don't think that he is alive anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. Well, Dr. Beslic is alive, or at least was when he testified. Did you try and talk with Dr. Beslic and say to him, I've got some questions about this old case of yours. Do you have a few minutes? Can we talk? Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So you simply went with the documents that we've seen here this morning, Defence 19; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And it is on the basis of those documents alone that you draw the conclusion that you do or the supposition that you do.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you did something somewhat similar in your analysis of the Markale marketplace shelling. You testified that you drew your conclusions based upon these photographs alone. Do you stand by that statement that you gave in your direct testimony?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Once again, you did not look at anything above and beyond these photographs. No medical documents, no telephone calls to Sarajevo to speak to the medical personnel concerned, just a view of the photographs; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reviewed the entire set of documents and there were only photographs there and a video footage. There was not a single medical document there, nor any reports on external examinations or autopsies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did it surprise you to find no such documentation, no written text documentation?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very much so, because it's mandatory to provide medical treatment and processing of all casualties or people who faced violent death.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did you make any efforts or any inquiries as to where these documents were and whether they could be made available to you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did try through the Defence counsel, and I insisted on being given any medical document, forensic medical document, on examination on any of the casualties to be provided for me in order to do my forensic analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did it concern you in terms of making conclusions that you did not have these documents? Were you concerned about going ahead in the absence of the information that you would expect to be contained in such documents?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it concerned me because a forensic medical examination in absence of this type of document is simply impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I have a moment to consult with my colleague?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was talking with Mr. Sachdeva because I believe that a number of medical documents related to Markale are in evidence and Mr. Sachdeva is going to look for the exhibit number and I'll apprise the Chamber once that's been found, if it's found.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: To state the obvious, Doctor, you are not the physician who conducted any of these examinations yourself. You did not see these victims with your own eyes.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And if we could please see Defence Exhibit 370, which is the first photograph that was shown to Dr. Milosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: This is the photograph that you made some markings on during your direct examination, Doctor, and your testimony -- let me just go through a couple of the points that you were talking about. It is your view, based on an analysis of the photograph alone, that some raised bumps on this man's face are shotgun pellets; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, let's talk just a little bit about how shotguns work. And I take it that you are -- in the course of your career, you've seen shotgun injuries and you've seen deaths caused by shotgun, haven't you? I'm sorry, sir, you have to answer out loud; otherwise, the court reporter doesn't get it.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Shotguns don't fire bullets, they fire cartridges, isn't that right, shotgun cartridges?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, and that's what I said in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm not saying that you testified differently. I'm just trying to establish some principles. And this cartridge is a tube made of some material that will give way when the shotgun is fired; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And inside that tube are thousands of tiny little pellets; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: When the tube falls away, the pellets stay in a tube shape for a while but then they start to disperse; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And some conclusions, more or less precise, more or less approximate, can be made about the range at which a shotgun was fired from the dispersal of these pellets; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, other material comes out the barrel of a shotgun as well; correct? Hot gases, for example, and perhaps even some of the powder that is used as the propellant; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: The effects of the hot gas and the propellant, however, are not felt very far from the shotgun. They fall away pretty quickly, don't they?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. And sometimes, by looking at a victim, if there are scorch marks from the hot gases or if some of the propellant is embedded in the victim, you know that this shotgun was fired from a very close range. That is one of the things that you can sometimes tell as a forensic pathologist; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, you testified on direct examination that this gentleman, in your opinion, was shot with a shotgun at a range of 50 centimetres. Do you stand by that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: At a range of 50 centimetres, the shotgun pellets, having fallen loose from the cartridge or having been released from the cartridge, are not very widely dispersed, are they?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And just to give us all an idea of what kind of a range we are talking about, when talking about Dzenana Sokolovic, you said that the width of a human abdomen was about 50 centimetres, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around that figure or more.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. I understand it's an approximation, but we're talking about something like hip to hip, okay? Doctor, if this individual had been shot at a range of 50 centimetres with a shotgun, I mean, he wouldn't have a face left, would he? At that range the shotgun pellets are still remarkably compact and carry an enormous amount of energy.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. At that distance shotgun pellets are still in a beam, which in this case hit the right-hand side of the neck corresponding to this wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And that would be that dark spot on the neck -- oh, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you just indicate to us 50 centimetres with your hands.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And, Witness, would you also -- I know you're not a ballistic expert, so not an expert in shotguns, but what -- if you were shooting with a shotgun at a distance of 50 centimetres, or less than a metre even, and you were shooting on a white piece of paper, what would be the range of the pellets at that distance? How big would the circle be that would include all the pellets? Can you -- if you know. As I said, I know that you're not an expert on these matters. But what would you expect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, the size of the circle depends on the angle. If one is shooting at a right angle, then the pellets disperse in a concentric shape around the wound. If it is at an angle, then they disperse upwards. Such a circle can be up to 10 centimetres big depending on the distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And in addition, Doctor, at a range of 50 centimetres, does it strike you as unusual that these pellets have done no more than insert themselves under the skin?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite to the contrary. The main beam, the main thrust, of the pellets made the wound in the neck. As for the other pellets which have lost their energy, which dispersed, they only penetrated subcutaneously in the region of the lower lip, the tip of the nose, and the left eyebrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Doctor, in the course of your career, have you ever handled a case of an individual who has committed suicide by shooting themselves in the head with a shotgun?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could you describe to Their Honours the degree of destruction of the victim's head when someone does that? In other words, talk to the Judges about what this close-range shotgun wound looks like.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
