utterances.text: When discussing suicide, what we have are usually the so-called contact wounds or wounds occurring at very short distances, up to 5 centimetres. One needs to distinguish between contact wounds, when the barrel is put against the body, and the wounds occurring at distances of less than 5 centimetres as opposed to the wounds created at larger distances of 50 centimetres or 1 metre. The difference is great, because with the contact wounds you also see burns caused by gases and gunpowder, whereas as you move away from the body, their effect is smaller or completely absent. Therefore, in cases of suicide we usually have contact wounds in question. When there is a contact wound in any given case from a shotgun or any other firearm, then we have a suspicion of a suicide. Forensically, medically speaking, such wounds can actually exhibit a large degree of destruction as opposed to the wounds of other types. And one also needs to distinguish between the relative distance from a hunting rifle and a firearm because there are differences there as well. We are talking here about a relative distance of 50 to 100 centimetres. We are not discussing the distance encountered with suicides. There we usually have contact wounds or very small distances away from the surface of the skin.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So there is a large degree of destruction. Is that the answer?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With such wounds, the degree of destruction is significant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, in this case we've got a man shot at what you are now describing as a 50- to 100-centimetre range, and the neck is, by and large, intact, is it not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the photograph we can only see the frontal part of the neck. We cannot speak about a general degree of destruction of the neck since we cannot see its rear side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you did not seek to find out if you could -- well, let me back up. You're saying that from this photograph you can't tell; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is it that I cannot tell?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I asked you about the degree of destruction of the neck and I believe that your answer, I'm paraphrasing, is, From this photograph I can't tell.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Based on this photograph one cannot discuss the degree of destruction of the neck.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And, again, you made no further inquiries. You simply used this photograph, as you said several times in your direct testimony, photograph alone; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked for all other documentation and was told that it is non-existent. In the documentation I received, information is rather scarce; therefore, whatever conclusions I may have arrived at, I arrived at by using this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you did not speak to the medical personnel concerned in Sarajevo, did you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Nor did you try to, did you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did through my lawyers. I tried to get some documentations. However, I was told it is not in existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, in the upper right-hand portion of this photograph you've circled several items, three of them in fact. Do you see what I am referring to?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the upper right-hand corner, the right-hand side of the photograph towards the top?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Two of those items have got a roughly circular shape; agreed?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They all have roughly circular shape.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And the one that is lowest down is rather long and sort of oval-shaped, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one do you have in mind? The lowest one? I encircled four; two towards the top and then two in the middle. One can see it much better on a plain photograph. This photograph has too many pixels. There are two up there and then three or even four further down below, and they are all circular and regular.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You say that there are three or even four. You can't tell if there are three or four from this picture, can you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this photograph on the screen one cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And it's your testimony that these are pellets that fell out of this man's head at the morgue but not before. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I suppose that one of the possible answers is that those pellets fell out of the exit wound, which is probably on the back of the neck, at the morgue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So that, again, is a supposition and in this case a possible supposition, to use your own words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did he say possible or professional?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I thought he said possible. At least that's what the English was. Page 49, line 4, it's at least been translated as a "possible answer."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh, no, I meant earlier in your cross-examination he described his supposition as professional.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm talking about another supposition now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That was the first supposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Counsel or Witness, may I just be sure that I understand this correctly: You're saying that the pellets that we see on the top right part of the photo could have dropped out of the exit wound, probably on the back of the head. Would that imply that they had gone through the skull of the victim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I said the back of the neck. Not the skull, the neck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So that the pellet would have gone in here and then out somewhere in the neck, through the neck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: But, Doctor, all of these things --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: But, Doctor, all of these things that you are testifying about are based upon the photograph; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: The concrete slab or wooden board upon which this victim is lying has got a lot of marks and a lot of discolouring on it, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Shrapnel is produced at an explosion when the bomb casing and other parts is broken up into many, many, many little pieces by the force of the explosion; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Shrapnel comes in all shapes and sizes, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not in the form of regular circular pellets.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What I'm asking, Doctor, is that shrapnel comes in --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Docherty, this photograph comes from you. Can I ask the question differently, phrase it differently. On the background where I see the three markings of these pellets, what you have called the pellets, is that a wall or is this the ground, is this the floor, in the morgue? Just a point of clarification, if I may. This is a question that I'm asking to the Prosecutor's Office because you have been producing this photograph. I cannot tell whether the background on which the head of the victim seems to be lying, is this a wall or is this the floor, the pavement or the floor, at the morgue? Because I can see the three markings made by those bullets or these pellets on this board, whatever it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, Judge Mindua, to answer -- I have a photograph that answers that question. It's obviously not on the list that I was going to use, but it is a photograph of the same victim but taken from the side, and you can see what he's lying on. And to answer your question, I'd ask, could we put this on the ELMO. It's part of the same packet of photographs. It's the immediately-preceding one. And although not directly responsive to your question, of course it's the Prosecution's -- you've described these as pellets, and it's the Prosecution's position these are not pellets at all. And, Judge Mindua, I don't want obviously to become a witness and talk much about this photograph, but I'll just note the correspondence in names down below in the typewritten area, and I'll also inquire if this answers the question that you were asking as to what the victim was lying on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It seems to me that he's lying on some sort of a table, on an autopsy table.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Again, I don't want to put myself in the position of testifying, but it looks like some sort of raised table, bench, something like that, yes. Could I tender that photograph, please, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P938, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, on this point that I'm talking about the doctor about now, I'm going to ask permission to use another photograph that was not on the list of documents, and if I could ask the usher to show this to Defence counsel and then, if they do not have an objection, to place it on the ELMO. It is another of the photographs from Markale.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, Doctor, have you seen this photograph before? Was it among the ones that you examined?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you understand that this is a photograph of various items of shrapnel collected at the Markale incident scene.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you would agree with me, would you not, that these shrapnel specimens vary in size and vary in shape, would you not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, amongst themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. I'm finished with that. Your Honour, I tender that photograph as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P300 -- I'm sorry, as P939, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: In addition to shrapnel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: One minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. President, before resuming, Mr. Sachdeva informs me that exhibits -- Prosecution Exhibits 71 through 82 on the spreadsheet of medical documentation admitted at page 48 of the transcript are -- excuse me, admitted as P48, so the spreadsheet is P48, and on there are found medical documents relating to the Markale incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: In addition to shrapnel at an explosion scene, Doctor, other things also fly through the air when things blow up, don't they? Cars, bits of market stalls, bits of human beings, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, depending on their distance from the centre of the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And people can die in explosions not just through shrapnel injuries but also through blast overpressure; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Through being crushed by an object that is displaced by the explosion; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And by burns; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Is that all of them or are there more?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are also the so-called blast injuries, injuries of internal organs that can only be detected by autopsy. They occur due to the overpressure at the site of explosion. They can damage blood vessels, vital organs, first and foremost, the brain and the intestines, causing massive haemorrhaging leading to death.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I meant to ask about that when I asked you if people can die through blast overpressure, but perhaps I didn't use the right term. I'd like to turn now to the next photograph that you made use of, which I believe would be Defence Exhibit 371. Now, Doctor, this again is a -- would it be fair to say that your testimony that this individual has been shot with a gun is another supposition based on the photograph alone?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my professional assumption based on this photograph and the photographs of bodies of people, or several hundreds of bodies of people that I saw in my career that were killed by firearms' projectiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And when you talk about the several hundred people you saw in your career, these are bodies that you saw yourself; right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You autopsied them; right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You collected, if appropriate, tissue samples and ran tests; right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in those cases that required it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If you wanted to, you had the opportunity to talk to the police officers who had done the initial investigation or to the investigating magistrate, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I even attended the scene myself on occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: But you didn't have the benefit of any of that when you made this professional assumption, did you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness' other microphone be turned on as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Gun-shot wounds, Doctor, can often be simple but sometimes they're tricky, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In exceptional cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: To take one of what might be the more common situations, if a bullet ricochets and is deformed, it will produce an entry wound that could be mistaken for an exit wound; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And there are other scenarios and, as you say, they are exceptional. But they happen, don't they?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And in this case, again, you are drawing, basing this professional assumption about a gun-shot wound on one photograph.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And then finally with respect to Markale, I'm going to ask for the video again and I'm going to ask the court registrar to stop the video at several time marks. The first of them is time mark number 8. Mr. President, I'm informed that because this is the Defence's video exhibit we don't have it in Sanction on our -- I'm sorry. [Videotape played]? It would be simpler if the Defence could please be asked to play it and stop at time mark 8. We've already gone past that, if we can move back to that. And then stop it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Doctor, this is the frame that you were testifying about, and we see this object in the foreground. Now, to be clear, you're using that object as a reference point. You're not saying there's anything significant about that object. It's just a way that we can tell where we are at the scene. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the way of limiting the area within which something is going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. It's a landmark.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you see in the background - it's a bit out of focus - but do you see a white car with two wheels in the street and the other two wheels up on the sidewalk?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And isn't that car blocking our view of anything that might be behind it, such as the lady's body that you testified about in your direct examination?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This car may block the view of what is happening behind it but not of what is happening in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Well, no, of course not. But -- well, we'll just -- we'll move on. Doctor, in the course of looking at this video you saw a very chaotic scene with a lot of injured and dead people being moved about. Is that a fair characterisation, a fair description?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I'm going to now move, with the Defence's assistance, to time mark 0.21, 21 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Doctor, here we see an individual, apparently wounded, being dragged, don't we?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Where are this person's hands and arms in relation to their body?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could we now move, please, to time mark 1 minute, 17 seconds, and that will be the last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Where are this lady's hands and arms in relation to her head, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The right arm is on the pavement above.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Above her head; right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, above her head.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. Suggesting that she, too, was dragged; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may have been the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. It may have been, Doctor - you don't know - that this woman was -- someone sought to help her and moved her a short distance by dragging her the way we saw the man being dragged; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there should also be marks present of the dragging.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Marks made by a -- well, first of all, Doctor, we can only see down to her feet, can't we?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in this frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: It's also possible - you can't say - that this woman suffered a fatal injury but lived for a certain period of time and that this is where she collapsed, in this position, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And finally, as you've said, it is possible that the vehicle that we saw at the 8-second time mark obscured our view of her, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One can say all this by looking at this frame. But by looking at the entire video, one can obtain much more details.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And later on when talking about the - excuse me - when talking about the area affected by this blast and by talking about the number of victims, you said one can estimate, one can guess, and given the information that you worked on, Doctor, that's really all that you've been able to do, isn't it, estimate and guess?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, based on this footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your evidence, Doctor, in a general way about Markale is an assertion that we cannot be sure that victims were killed somewhere else and then brought to the marketplace; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we also cannot be sure that all the victims died at the scene of the crime, which is depicted in this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Are you aware, Doctor, that other Defence witnesses - and I'm speaking now about Mr. Demurenko - have said -- have explained the Markale marketplace by saying that there was an explosion but that it wasn't a mortar shell in the marketplace. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. So Mr. Demurenko says there was an explosion and that killed the people and you say the people were brought here from somewhere else. Do you see the contradiction there, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I already said that the film shows that there had been an explosion and there were some casualties, but I cannot say clearly for every single victim that he or she died there, primarily having in mind this victim that we have just seen on the footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you base that upon the fact that this victim is not visible at the 8-second time mark but is visible here at the 1 minute, 17-second time mark. Is that what you base that upon?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only that but also the absence of blood marks where the victim is lying and the marks of the victim being dragged, if she had been dragged at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Doctor, under this victim there is -- under this victim's head the frame is quite dark, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. Blood marks within that dark area would not be visible on the video, would they?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this frame. But if you look at the entire video, there are some sequences where you have a close-up look of her face and her chest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think we'll have to take the break now, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, over the break I had a chance to review my notes and at this point I have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Doctor, before we move to the re-examination, I'd like to just clarify a few things so as to allow the Defence to come back on the information that is offered to you by virtue of my questions. Could we revert to Defence Exhibit D370, if I can ask the Defence to pull up that picture again. I don't know, I don't have it. I have a blue screen on my -- there it comes. Great. Doctor, I have two questions relating to this picture. The first is the two objects that you have identified as pellets, or possibly as pellets, on the top right side of the picture, and the difficulty I have with accepting your proposal that these are pellets is the size of them. I would imagine that pellets in a cartridge were much smaller and even -- even the largest pellets that I have seen are far from the size of these two objects. They would be even less than half of the size. So I would like you to explain how you come to the conclusion that these are pellets. And the difficulty I have, as I said, is the size. The second question I have to you is in continuation of your answer to me about how big the diameter of the circle would be that would include all the pellet marks shot from a distance of less than 1 metre with a shotgun, and you answered correctly that that would depend, of course, on the angle, but that if shot at a perpendicular angle, the circle would be 10 centimetres in diameter. A cartridge contains several hundred pellets and if you were to put all these pellets into a circle of approximately 10 centimetres, the distance between them would be very small. And according to your own suggestion, the face of the victim has three, four, or maybe five pellets scattered throughout his face and this simply seems to be incompatible with your own suggestion that all the pellets would be found within the circle of a 10-centimetre diameter. So either these are not pellets from a shotgun or the distance must have been much, much larger, in my interpretation of your answer. Could you please clarify these two questions for me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the look and the size of the pellets, we saw a while ago the photograph of various shrapnel found and photographed at the scene, ranging from the smallest one to the biggest one, and we could clearly see that none of these pieces of shrapnel resembles in the shape or the size of the pellets that we see in this photograph. I am not a ballistic expert or an expert in weapons and ammunition, but my estimate is based primarily on the dozens of fatalities ensuing from the injuries caused from shotguns. I also saw dozens or maybe even a hundred people injured by hand-grenades that also contained pellets inside its body. These pellets are much smaller and they're always very small, 1 to 2 millimetres in diameter. Based on my professional experience regarding the size of these pellets, on many an occasion I saw, because there are different sized pellets than here we have the ones that are 3 to 4 millimetres in diameter, not more, and I think this is the answer to your first question. Concerning your second question, after firing the directed beam of pellets travels in a straight line and most of them cause the wound, as we can see here, the wound in the right-hand side of the neck. The pellets placed centripetally in regard to an imaginary circle of the beam disperse because they lose energy during the flight. This dispersion can take place laterally with regard to the main wound, up to 10 centimetres depending on the range, and it's concentric if the shot was fired at 90 degrees. If the shot, however, was fired at a different angle with regard to the body and to the entry wound, then the dispersion tends to go more to one side. My assumption here was that the dispersion was -- or that the bullet was fired from the side and from down, therefore dispersing the pellets upwards towards the face. Since we have the face and we have an angle, some of them dispersed in an area and only individual pellets hit the most prominent parts of the face, that is to say, parts of the face that created an obstacle in their path. Looking at this photograph, the shape and the size of these lumps on the skin, as I described them, would correspond to the pellets that we see on the right-hand side in terms of their size.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. And it is your suggestion or estimation that the lumps we see on the nose and under the lip are lumps that include a pellet underneath; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and on the right eyebrow as well. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Milosavljevic, when in June, after I had to sever contacts with an expert witness and I discussed this issue with you in June and you accepted to undertake the responsibility to prepare this report for the Defence, can you tell me, when I asked you whether you wanted to carry out your professional job in the spirit and ethical norms applicable when you do these kind of assignments, what did you request from me in order to enable you to provide a solid and valid expert report and as you customarily do whenever somebody seeks your assistance?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I primarily asked for proper forensic and medical documents, that is to say, autopsy reports and external examination reports. I also asked for medical records relating to the treatment of the injured and the final outcome of the treatment. And only after that, of course, I asked, in addition to all of that, to be given police documentation relating to the investigations carried out with regard to these specific incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And when I told you that I don't have autopsy reports or external examination reports, nor the photographs from the place or the traces of blood from the scene at my disposal, nor the established time of death, when I told you all of this, what did you say to me?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that in the absence of these kind of documents I absolutely cannot prepare a valid forensic report and cannot give answers to the crucial questions relating to this incident. The only thing I could do was to tell you what the significance of forensic medical examination is and what procedures are applied, and particularly how important an investigation of the crime scene is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When I told you that I could only give you a medical report stating somebody's death and that I had a document that something was described as a serious bodily injury and nothing apart from that, what did you tell me how useful that would be for you to give an expert opinion?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document verifying and confirming death can simply tell us only that a person has died and that he or she is not alive anymore. Probably if it contains the diagnosis of death, one can assume the cause of death and nothing more in terms of what I explained earlier. Such a document cannot be used for a proper forensic and medical report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You will remember that I asked you, and I believe that it was possible, based on such scarce documents, were you able to tell whether a person was killed in a certain location?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that it was absolutely impossible because that would require a complete forensic investigation and a complete forensic and medical analysis in order to compile all the results, make certain comparisons, and establish the cause-and-effect relations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now look at the Prosecution Exhibit P939, which shows pieces of shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let us look at these pieces of shrapnel. They vary in size. Does any of these pieces of shrapnel, and particularly the last three ones and actually the last and the smallest ones, could this kind of piece of shrapnel cause the injuries on the face of the witness shown in the photograph D371 or the one shown in the photograph 370? Can you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, what you see, that in all its variety, none of these pieces of shrapnel resembles the pellets that we see in the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Speaking of pellets, I know nothing about their sizes and I especially have no idea about the number of pellets in the cartridge. That is why we have people who are experts in this field. You said if it comes at an angle it disperses upwards, but these pellets disperse in other directions as well when the shot is fired upwards.

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that pellets, the ones that lose their energy and are on the periphery of the beam, disperse depending on the angle vertically and horizontally. Therefore, they may go vertically upwards or to the side with respect to the centre of the wound hit by the directed beam of pellets.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If the body was lying horizontally and with regards to everything else you said about the pellets, how is it possible -- well, is there any other rational explanation for those pellets to be there, apart from the one you've provided, the pellets that were next to the head of the victim on both sides?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are talking about the pellets next to the head on the table. We saw that it is a table of sorts on that additional photo we saw. Since this was a body lying on a table, the possibility is even greater that the pellets fell out of that particular body rather than being there from some previous victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So as not to go back to the footage and if we use the assumption stated by my learned friend Mr. Docherty that the woman may have staggered to that place and then fallen down, that she covered some distance while still alive, would in that case there be some blood traces behind her and is it possible not to have a pool of blood underneath her body?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that person had sustained injuries, first of all, that person must have walked up to that spot. There was that part of the footage where there are no victims in that part of the street and then after that, there is a body. The sequence is very short between the first and second instance. Therefore, the person recording had to move towards the centre of explosion. Therefore, I believe in the movement the camera would have caught such a person moving towards it. On the other hand, if that person was moving from the place of explosion where she may have been injured, the traces of blood spraying would be visible during the entire length of the path she crossed, and especially in the very spot she fell down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: My last question is this: Having in mind the distance in metres and the camera observing it all and comparing that to the time that elapses, which is less than a minute, you said that if that victim was walking that would have been recorded and that there would have been traces. What if that body was dragged?

utterances.speaker: IVICA MILOSAVLJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is fully justified to suppose that she may have been dragged, but had she been dragged, that would have been recorded on the footage as well because the person with the camera was moving towards the place of explosion, recording the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to thank Their Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Doctor, that concludes your evidence, and we thank you for giving it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, is that the case for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had no translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I was asking if that is the case for the Defence. Was that your last witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This concludes the Defence case. We have no further witnesses. And I'd like to thank you on behalf of this Defence team for having given us the possibility to state our case and for you to see the evidence that we wanted to present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And on behalf of the Chamber, I'd like to thank both parties for the presentation of their cases and for the manner in which the cases were presented. The Chamber will, after hearing the closing arguments, deliberate and give its judgement. As you know, the final briefs are due on Monday, the 1st of October, and closing arguments were set for Monday, the 8th and Tuesday, the 9th, and the Chamber is now resetting those dates to Wednesday, the 10th and Thursday, the 11th of October. There are a number of matters which I wish to raise. At the start of the case the Prosecution said it intended to tender a DVD with all videos taken of the witnesses and the Prosecution investigator, but during the case for the Prosecution, not all videos contained on the DVD have been shown and tendered. Does the Prosecution wish to tender all the videos that were shown in court into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Yes, we do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Monkhouse reminded me of this in an e-mail last week. The issue that we've got is that each victim has got two interviews. One of them we call the long form where the investigator reads out GPS coordinates, for example; one of them shorter. What I need to do is go back through and see which ones were played in court and tender just those. So if it was the long one that was played, tender the long one; if it was the short one, tender the short one. We can do this in one of two ways and I'll be guided by the Chamber. I have the 65 ter numbers and I could tender all the videos at this time and then later move to withdraw those that were not played in court, or by written submission later this week could ask for just those that were played in court to be admitted. And I'll take the Chamber's guidance on whichever route they wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The latter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That was quick. Very well. We'll take care of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The next matter was the 92 bis statement of Witness 109. It has not been included in e-court. This statement was admitted by the Chamber's decision of the 3rd of April. Is the Prosecution in a position to clarify what the status of this exhibit is?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: We are, Your Honour. At the close of the Prosecution case, Mr. Whiting read off -- let me back up. On the 3rd of April, 2007, the 92 bis statement of Witness 109 was admitted with the registry later to give it an exhibit number. It then developed that the Prosecution wished not to call this witness for reasons having to do with the relevance of this witness' testimony. At the conclusion of the Prosecution case, Mr. Whiting read off a list of 92 bis and 92 quater witnesses. This list did not include Witness 109. We had thought that that would let the Chamber know that we were not persisting in seeking to admit this. It develops that our communication was not as clear as we had hoped and so at this time I can tell the Chamber that we are withdrawing, we will not call, Witness 109, and that statement should not be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thanks for the clarification. I am to let you know that the recording of the comments of the parties during the site visit is being transcribed and as soon as that is done the Chamber will give a decision on the admission of the document. Any matters to raise, Mr. Tapuskovic? Housekeeping.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. My learned friend Ms. Isailovic had to leave, although she wanted to address you on her behalf regarding this issue. However, she put some things in writing that we will present you with and you will rule on that. First of all, we have the three 92 bis statements and we are still seeking certification from the registrar. There is also a motion in place concerning a number of adjudicated facts in the Galic case. This was submitted in writing. Also, there is a list of documents introduced through our witness, through one of our witnesses. The translation of those documents is now completed and we are still awaiting translation of those documents that are outstanding and then you can rule on that issue as well. At this stage I can only tell you that this is what remains to be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. As for the motion on adjudicated facts, I can let you know that we will give our decision on that before the end of this week. What is the first matter you mentioned, 92 bis statements in respect of which you are still seeking certification from the registrar? What's that about?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are three statements of that nature. What is even more important for us are the documents that you cannot decide upon until their translations are completed. Some of the translation has already been done and we forwarded a list of the documents with complete translations, and I believe you are to rule on the use of those documents once you had an opportunity to view them. These documents should have been introduced through Witness T-35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I have a recollection of that. And when we have the translation we will issue a ruling. Mr. Docherty, any other matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: None, Your Honour. I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm to thank all of you for the help that you've given the Chamber in this matter, and we will be looking forward to receiving the closing briefs and, of course, the closing arguments shortly thereafter. Thank you. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
